messages.content: I'm planning a camping trip and I need to know the weather forecast. Can you fetch me the weather data for the campsite located at latitude 35. and longitude for the next 10 days including daily temperature and precipitation forecasts? Also, I prefer the temperature 2 minute max in Fahrenheit and sum of precipitation in inches. Don't give me hourly information

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

Sure! To get the 10‑day forecast for your campsite, I just need one more piece of information:

**What is the longitude of the campsite?**

Once I have that, I’ll pull the daily maximum temperature (in °F) and total precipitation (in inches) for the next 10 days.

The user wants weather forecast for next 10 days, daily temperature and precipitation forecasts. They want temperature 2 minute max in Fahrenheit and sum of precipitation in inches. They don't want hourly info.

We have a tool `requests_get` that can call Open-Meteo API. We need to construct a request to get daily data for temperature_2m_max in Fahrenheit and precipitation_sum in inches. The Open-Meteo API supports units=imperial for Fahrenheit and inches. For daily variables, we can request daily=temperature_2m_max,precipitation_sum. We also need to specify timezone maybe. The API endpoint is something like "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast". We need to pass params: latitude, longitude, daily=..., timezone=... etc. The user gave latitude 35. and longitude ??? The user wrote "latitude 35. and longitude for the next 10 days". They didn't provide longitude. Possibly they omitted. We need to ask for missing longitude. But the instruction says "Don't give me hourly information." We can still ask for missing longitude. The user might have omitted. We should ask for the missing longitude. The user said "latitude 35. and longitude for the next 10 days". That seems incomplete. So we should ask for the longitude. According to policy, we can ask clarifying question. So we will ask: "Could you please provide the longitude?"
